plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This holds because your payment only depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you're the winner), so shading your bid only risks losing profitable wins without any benefit. Bidding above value risks winning at a loss; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $28.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This holds because the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid, so misrepresenting your value only risks losing profitable trades or winning unprofitable ones. Since my value is $23, bidding exactly $23 maximizes expected profit: I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and pay only that amount, ensuring non-negative surplus whenever I win.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with 3 bidders, where bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, there's no incentive to shade my bid below or above my true valuation of $36. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to me; underbidding risks losing an item I'd profit from. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.
